sentences.text: Revenue compounded 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].

FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge [F13][D97][X112], which the FY2020 filing attributes to currency devaluations and decelerating grooming category growth [P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% to $15.7 billion, $8.3 billion of the increase being the base-period Shave Care charge [F14][D148][P71].
Since then the shape is slow compounding: revenue grew 2.0% a year over FY2023..FY2026 [D664], and operating margin has held between 22.1% and 24.3% [F27][F29].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing 4.0pp of FY2020 revenue growth and 2.2pp in FY2024 [D518][D530].
In FY2026 the mix flipped: Non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added 0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
Fabric & Home Care, 34.8% of revenue, added 0.8pp, with net sales up 2% on favorable foreign exchange of 1% and pricing of 1% [D541][D543][P12].
Beauty added 1.3pp as net sales rose 7.1%, led by Personal Care and Hair Care volume growth from innovation [D601][D602][D603][P20][P21].
Profit did not keep pace: operating income fell 3.4% against 3.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of -25.6% [D458][D457][D481].
Operating margin of 22.7% in FY2026 sits just above the window median of 22.1%, well off the FY2025 high of 24.3% and far above the FY2019 low of 8.1% [F30][D648][D647][D646].
The 1.6pp decline came from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp), as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and marketing spending rose [D470][D483][D485][P25][P5].
Cost of revenue rose 5.3% against 3.3% revenue growth, lifting it to 49.8% of revenue from 48.8% [D472][D457][D435][D384].
Below the line, other non-operating income of $1.1 billion, up $922 million on the Glad joint-venture dissolution gain, held net margin at 18.4% despite the operating decline [X108][P24][F50].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, against a window median of 1.02x [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
The 9.8% operating cash flow increase came mostly from net earnings, while inventory consumed $641 million and payables generated $919 million [D462][P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is in line with the 17.2% window median but below the 20.5% FY2021 high [D441][D654][D653].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, the highest capital intensity in the window [D464][F90][D440][D446].
Net debt of $24.2 billion is 27.8% of revenue, far more levered than the staples peer median of -1.0% net cash, ranking in the 33rd percentile of six peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median, and long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [F180][D663][F190][D468].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [X134][X144][D453][D476].
Return on average equity of 30.1% is strong in absolute terms but only the 33rd percentile against six peers, reflecting a large equity base rather than weak profitability [D456][D680].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window, at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][F171].
This is structural for a negative-working-capital consumer staples business, not a liquidity event, given $9.9 billion of cash and steady free cash flow [F140][F100].
Payout exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% respectively [D402][D453].
That leaves little room if free cash flow dips, and the gap has been closed partly by debt rather than by cash generation [D453][D450].
Operating margin: a print below the 22.1% window median would confirm the FY2026 cost pressure, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high would reverse it [D648][D647].
Free cash flow margin: holding at or above the 17.2% median would keep the payout covered, while a drop toward the 14.4% FY2017 low would strain it [D654][D652].
Capex: watch whether it stays near the 5.1% of revenue seen in FY2026 or falls back toward the 3.7% FY2021 level [D440][D182].
